purpose: Classify whether first-published / historical-vintage Macro Core values can be reconstructed from official sources before declaring the historical panel FULL_PIT.

status_classes.STRUCTURED_VINTAGE_AVAILABLE: Official source exposes a real-time/vintage/revision-history dataset suitable for programmatic reconstruction.
status_classes.ARCHIVED_RELEASE_RECOVERABLE: Official dated releases/archive exist and appear capable of recovering first-published values, but extraction must be done release-by-release and value-level matched.
status_classes.REVISED_HISTORY_ONLY_UNTIL_PROVEN: Current historical series is revised and no first-release recovery mechanism has yet been verified.
status_classes.SERIES_MATCH_PENDING: Official vintage/release mechanism exists, but exact runtime-series identity still needs value/key matching.

findings.evidence: BEA current releases explicitly state that original data are retained in the BEA Data Archive after later releases supersede them; current pages also document revisions.
Federal Reserve publishes revision-history data containing the initially published index and one- through six-month subsequent vintages, plus previous releases/historical release dates.
Census maintains historical Advance Monthly Retail Trade releases by month/year and annual revision reports; historical releases are explicitly not overwritten by current data.

findings.family: Census Manufacturers' Orders / Core Capital Goods
findings.evidence: Release family is known, but a structured first-release vintage dataset for the exact stored core-capital-goods transformation has not yet been verified in this audit.
Dated historical Employment Situation releases are the intended reconstruction path; value-level extraction and revision sequencing still need to be materialized.
Dated JOLTS releases are the intended reconstruction path; exact first-published values have not yet been loaded into the PIT panel.
Dated Productivity and Costs releases can be used; exact vintage extraction pending.
U.S. Department of Labor maintains weekly Claims releases/archives. First-published weekly values must be taken from the dated release rather than the latest revised history.
Eurostat publishes vintage datasets for industrial production with historical release vintages.
Eurostat publishes vintage datasets for unemployment with historical release vintages.
Dated Euro-indicator releases exist; unlike unemployment/IP, retail trade was not confirmed in this audit as part of Eurostat's structured vintage database.
Dated Eurostat releases exist; structured vintage support for this exact stored series was not confirmed.
ECB negotiated-wage datasets/release history exist; the exact runtime series key/value match must be certified before vintage reconstruction.

findings.family: ONS Production / Retail / Labour Market / PAYE
findings.evidence: ONS release calendar and archived releases preserve dated publications. ONS also uses real-time databases and revision triangles for some economic statistics, demonstrating an explicit vintage framework, but exact real-time tables for every one of these five runtime series must still be checked.

Statistics Bureau warns that current historical data are revised, while annual reports preserve figures as of publication. This gives a source path for historical vintages but requires publication-by-publication extraction.
METI distinguishes preliminary and revised releases. Historical first-release values should be reconstructed from preliminary releases, with revised releases treated as later information events.
Official provisional/final release mechanism has been identified, but the precise runtime production-series variant still needs value-level matching.
Official releases distinguish provisional and later final results; dated provisional releases are the intended PIT source.
Monthly official labour-market releases are dated, but exact seasonally-adjusted/unadjusted runtime variant must be certified.
Official Employment Barometer releases are dated; first-release extraction pending.

findings.family: Statistics Canada Monthly GDP by Industry
findings.evidence: Statistics Canada table 36-10-0491-01 is explicitly a historical real-time table designed to track estimates since initial release.
Dated The Daily releases and historical/real-time table opportunities exist; exact table matching for the runtime volume measure still needs to be materialized.
Dated The Daily releases preserve contemporary estimates; exact revision/vintage extraction still pending.
ABS documents regular and historical revisions and retains previous releases; first-published quarterly estimates should be reconstructed from the release archive, not current revised history.
Dated ABS release pages are available; first-release extraction pending.
Dated ABS Labour Force releases are available; current series may embody revisions and seasonal re-estimation, so release-vintage extraction is required.
Dated ABS WPI releases are available; value-level first-release extraction pending.

findings.family: Stats NZ GDP / Retail / Labour Market
findings.evidence: Stats NZ maintains dated information releases. First-published values can potentially be reconstructed release-by-release; a structured real-time database was not verified in this audit.
Dated RBNZ survey releases are the intended source, but these stored series currently have fewer than 8 observations and therefore do not enter normalizedSeriesImpulse yet.

summary.conclusion: A full PIT panel appears feasible for a large majority of the Core Macro set, but most series require archive-level extraction rather than a ready-made real-time database. The panel is not yet FULL_PIT_READY.

next_action: Build actual first-release values for the 4 structured-vintage series first.
Resolve the 3 exact-series matches and the US core-capital-goods vintage path.
For archived-release families, extract only the observations needed at monthly model checkpoints from 2020-08 onward rather than reconstructing every calendar day.
Run a revised-vs-first-release sensitivity comparison before deciding whether any REVISED_ONLY series can remain in the historical test.
